Baseline, 3-month and 12-month follow-up. The source file is wide, with the wave encoded in the column prefix (pb / pm / py); the tidier reshapes it to one row per pupil per wave and drops the 541 pupil-waves where no follow-up questionnaire was returned.

No collection date is in the data. SEYLE recruited between Nov 2009 and Dec 2010 (10.1016/S0140-6736(14)61213-7; protocol 10.1186/1471-2458-10-192), placing baseline and the 3-month follow-up in 2009-2010 and the 12-month follow-up in 2010-2011. 2010 / 2010 / 2011 is the best single-year approximation for the German site and should be confirmed with the data provider; some baseline pupils will have been surveyed in 2009.

SEYLE is a four-arm cluster-randomised trial (10.1016/S0140-6736(14)61213-7). No arm variable is released, but character 7 of the pupil ID is one of Q/A/P/C followed by a two-digit school number, and the four letters match the published arms - QPR gatekeeper training, the Awareness / Youth Aware of Mental Health workshops, ProfScreen professional screening, and the minimal-intervention Control - in roughly equal quarters (Q 330, A 368, P 423, C 323 pupils, each letter nested in distinct schools). The decode is inferred from the ID and is not documented in the codebook: confirm with the data provider before use. Screen use was not manipulated by any arm, so the cohort is in scope under DR-0001.

Age in whole years is recorded once, at baseline (12-21, median 15). Follow-up ages are the baseline age plus the nominal follow-up interval, so they carry up to a year of error and are non-integer at the 3-month wave; partial for that reason. One pupil reports 21 at baseline and so exceeds the schema's 0-19 range at every wave - flagged rather than silently dropped.
Pupil self-report; only codes 1 and 2 occur and there is no missingness (692 male, 752 female).

notes: Ethnicity is never asked. The migration block records citizenship and country of birth for the pupil and both parents, including free-text country names (most commonly Turkey, Kazakhstan, Russia, Poland, Kosovo). Country of birth is not ethnicity, and the schema's White/Black/Asian/Hispanic vocabulary maps badly onto German migration categories - ethnic-German repatriates from Kazakhstan and Russia and Turkish-origin pupils are the two largest groups and neither has a defensible destination. Migration background is carried in minority instead.
